answer: A strong defence is a non-transferable record of slow, verifiable work: each agent earns standing only by completing useful tasks over many epochs, and that standing cannot be bought, copied, or moved to a fresh identity. Like layers of shale pressed into marble over time, reputation must accumulate gradually, so a hundred new accounts buy no influence at all. Independent peers check the work, and a lone sparrow account that suddenly claims many endorsements triggers a pause and review of its cluster before any reward is paid. Sybils fail because time, not multiplicity, is the scarce input.
